goals.headline: Descriptive, n=2 per prompt. At the 128K cap: code all tests pass 7/8 on both engines (217 vs 212 of 218 tests, vLLM fork v0.9.2 vs CuteAFD v3.0.1), MATH-500 level 5 8/8 on both (ceiling), prose 8/8 stopped on both, JSON valid 6/8 vs 4/8; CuteAFD replies ran ~15-25% shorter (median prose 39K vs 49K, code 38K vs 51K tokens), cause not separated from sampling. Code 'terminal loop' flags (vLLM 6 at L3 and 1 at L3s, CuteAFD 2 at L2 and 4 at L3) have no exact period; the audit (U5) read vLLM's as the answer restating code drafted in the reasoning; at the L1/L2 caps and for the 1,030-record JSON task the cells measure stop-versus-cap, not task completion.

goals.question: Was vLLM's run-to-run variation on the precision panels correctly attributed and sized?

design.instrument: separate read-only review by a reviewer who did not run the measurements; CPU recomputation from captures, logs and source in network-less containers (recomputation scripts not published)
design.items: P-B windows by number of prefill steps; full-vocabulary dumps (34 windows, gen rows)
design.n: 64 P-B windows; 34 windows for the full-vocabulary split

goals.headline: Every vLLM capture ran alone with identical chunking, so the variation is not batching or speculation: generated rows are 100% bit-equal between V1 and V1r in 1-step windows, 46% in 2-step and 0% in 4+ step windows; vLLM's self-divergence is 55% (2-8K) and 65% (8-16K) of the cross-engine KL. Against mean(V1, V1r), 8-16K KL +0.0050 [+0.0031, +0.0071], top-1 −0.87 [−1.20, −0.54]; the 2-8K top-1 +0.39 [+0.03, +0.76] against V1 is +0.14 [−0.29, +0.48] against V1r (not detected).

goals.question: Did Block T give both engines identical inputs?

design.instrument: separate read-only review by a reviewer who did not run the measurements; CPU recomputation from captures, logs and source in network-less containers (recomputation scripts not published)
design.items: 1,008 paired Block T requests; 128K code prompts

goals.headline: No: 0 of 1,008 paired requests share a nonce (salt includes the run label and time), so prompts differ in their first line; seeds still pair. The 128K code prompts are 24 tokens longer on CuteAFD v3.0.1 because the vLLM stack parses literal <think> and </think> in user text as special tokens and CuteAFD keeps them as text, so A2's 'same prompt' does not hold for those cells; the audit reads the throughput impact as negligible.

goals.question: Is the P-B gap 'located at 8-16K and growing with context', or confounded with content?

design.instrument: separate read-only review by a reviewer who did not run the measurements; CPU recomputation from captures, logs and source in network-less containers (recomputation scripts not published)
design.items: P-B generated rows by block and bucket
design.n: 18 windows at 8-16K (12 block B, 6 block A)
design.interval: window bootstrap; Bonferroni 99.67% intervals over about 15 looks; leave-one-window-out

goals.headline: Confounded: all 12 block-B (long code reading) windows sit at 8-16K and supply 6,144 of its 7,522 rows. Within block A, C1 − mean(V) KL is 0-2K +0.0029 [−0.0013, +0.0083], 2-8K +0.0017 [−0.0005, +0.0033], 8-16K +0.0028 [−0.0003, +0.0055], difference-in-differences +0.0006 [−0.0030, +0.0044]: growth with context not detected for KL. The 8-16K difference survives leave-one-window-out (+0.0037 to +0.0051) and Bonferroni (KL +0.0044 [+0.0003, +0.0082]); headlining the bucket was post hoc framing.

goals.question: Does the FP8 mechanism story (projections, head, KDA) cover the engines' arithmetic differences, and is F1a a clean ablation?

design.instrument: separate read-only review by a reviewer who did not run the measurements; CPU recomputation from captures, logs and source in network-less containers (recomputation scripts not published)
design.items: source, launch logs, dry-runs; P-B gen-row entropies

goals.headline: Narrowed: the engines also differ in DSA index-key format (CuteAFD BF16 keys, vLLM FP8), attention placement, KDA split path, prefill geometry, BF16 logits in vLLM and W8A8 prefill (source and logs, not measured); F1a also drops KDA output sharding, and F1's reading rule is ambiguous. CuteAFD's predictive entropy is higher (8-16K 0.580 vs V1 0.523, 18 of 18 windows); the audit infers, untested, a scale or bias effect rather than zero-mean rounding.

goals.question: Do Q2's sub-results (per-type NLL, '3x' run-to-run ratio) hold with 6 documents?

design.instrument: separate read-only review by a reviewer who did not run the measurements; CPU recomputation from captures, logs and source in network-less containers (recomputation scripts not published)
design.items: Q2 per-window results
design.interval: t-intervals on document means (5 and 2 df)

goals.headline: Overall C1 − V1 NLL −0.0005, t-interval [−0.0046, +0.0035]; prose +0.0019 [−0.0013, +0.0050], code −0.0029 [−0.0135, +0.0077]: neither sub-claim excludes 0. One window (c2-064k) dominates code; on matched documents the engine disagreement is 1.8x vLLM's floor, not 3x. Q2 can bound an NLL difference at about 0.004-0.005 nat, so only a bounded statement is supported.

goals.question: Do P-B's trailing context rows show a reference-side error?

design.instrument: separate read-only review by a reviewer who did not run the measurements; CPU recomputation from captures, logs and source in network-less containers (recomputation scripts not published)
design.items: 30 trailing spans in tool-call windows

goals.headline: All 30 trailing spans are near-copies of one unrelated filler file, so effectively one item; cross-engine KL on rows 20+ into the span is 0.72 / 3.14 / 2.53 nats on three windows and vLLM-vs-itself 1.96 nats on a10. The audit reads this as hypersensitive rows, not evidence of a reference-side error.

goals.question: Is Block T protected against drift and thermal or clock variation?

design.instrument: separate read-only review by a reviewer who did not run the measurements; CPU recomputation from captures, logs and source in network-less containers (recomputation scripts not published)
design.items: Block T run order, pre-run GPU snapshots, F1-base vs C1-r1 cells

goals.headline: No drift control (no declared CVC subset; V ran before C, no repeat) and no in-run telemetry. F1-base against C1-r1 gives per-cell ratios 0.96-1.08 on decode and 0.96-1.05 on aggregate, so single-cell noise is about ±4-8% and T-SUMMARY ratios between 0.95 and 1.08 cannot be read as differences; T-SUMMARY has no intervals.

design.instrument: separate read-only review by a reviewer who did not run the measurements; CPU recomputation from captures, logs and source in network-less containers (recomputation scripts not published)
arms: C1 (DFlash2 adaptive, FP8 drafter, W8A8 draft linear)

goals.headline: Draft policies differ (vLLM 3 fixed BF16 draft tokens; CuteAFD adaptive with an FP8 drafter and W8A8 draft linear) and acceptance was not recorded; the audit reads the 1.16-1.41x on code, json and reasoning vs 1.02-1.06 on prose as consistent with deeper drafting on predictable text.
